{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when price is trending downward — avoid over-optimism.",
    "When true outcome spikes sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day), reduce forecast overshoot by 10–20% to prevent overreaction.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "In late periods (e.g., last 5 days of forecast), increase downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative — prices often consolidate or reverse.",
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.25), allow slight upward bias but cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high to avoid overestimating momentum.",
    "When true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect underperformance bias.",
    "In high-sentiment periods, avoid forecasting sharp reversals — use smoother trend lines to prevent false signals."
  ]
}
